items.title: A patient signs in with a phone number and a code
items.description_md: A patient opens the BrightSmile website on their phone, enters their mobile number and receives a 6-digit code by SMS. Entering the code signs them in. A phone number the system has not seen before becomes a new account once the code is verified and the patient has typed their name. Wrong or expired codes are explained plainly and a new code can be asked for. After 5 wrong tries the patient must wait 15 minutes. The patient stays signed in for 7 days from their last use so they do not need a new SMS every visit. Why this priority: without patient sign-in no patient can book, which is the main goal of the product (booking online instead of by phone). It is also the only part of the system that costs money per use (SMS), so its limits matter from day one. Independent test: with a fake SMS sender, request a code for a phone number, read it from the fake sender, verify it, and see a signed-in session; repeat with a wrong code 5 times and see the 15-minute wait. Fully testable without any booking feature.

user_story.i_want: to sign in with my mobile number and a 6-digit code sent by SMS, and be registered on first use with my name
user_story.so_that: I can book and manage visits without a password or a phone call, and stay signed in for 7 days

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a phone number that already has an account, When the patient asks for a code and enters the correct code within 10 minutes, Then the patient is signed in and sees their name
Given a phone number with no account, When the patient enters the correct code, Then the system asks for their name, and after the name is given an account is created and the patient is signed in
Given a code was sent, When the patient enters a wrong code, Then the system says the code is wrong, says how many tries are left, and offers to send a new code
Given a code was sent more than 10 minutes ago, When the patient enters it, Then the system says the code has expired and offers a new code

Given a patient has entered 5 wrong codes for a phone number, When they try again or ask for a new code within 15 minutes, Then the system refuses and says when they can try again; after 15 minutes they can ask for a new code
Given a signed-in patient who last used the site 6 days ago, When they open the site, Then they are still signed in
Given a signed-in patient who last used the site more than 7 days ago, When they open the site, Then they must sign in again

Given too many codes were requested from one network address in a short time, or the daily limit of codes for one phone number is used up, When another code is requested, Then the system refuses without sending an SMS and says to try later or phone the clinic

items.title: Staff sign in with a username and password
items.description_md: A receptionist, dentist or practice manager opens the staff sign-in page, enters a username and password and lands on the screen for their role. Passwords have at least 10 characters. After 5 wrong passwords in a row the account is locked for 15 minutes. Staff sessions end after 8 hours, or after 30 minutes without use. **Why this priority**: Reception, dentists and the manager cannot work without it, and the other staff stories (roles, account management) depend on it. **Independent Test**: Create a staff account in the database (seed or admin tool), sign in with the right password, fail 5 times with a wrong one and see the lock, and check that a session idle for 30 minutes is refused. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an active staff account, **When** the person enters the correct username and password, **Then** they are signed in and the system tells the web app their role and (for receptionists) their clinic. 2. **Given** an active staff account, **When** the person enters a wrong password, **Then** the system says the username or password is wrong, without saying which one. 3. **Given** 5 wrong passwords in a row for one username, **When** the person tries again within 15 minutes (even with the right password), **Then** the sign-in is refused with a message that the account is locked and for how long. 4. **Given** a password shorter than 10 characters, **When** it is set for a staff account, **Then** the system rejects it and says the minimum length. 5. **Given** a signed-in staff member idle for 30 minutes, or signed in for 8 hours, **When** they make a request, **Then** the session is refused and they must sign in again. 6. **Given** a signed-in user, **When** they sign out, **Then** the session ends at once and cannot be reused. ---

user_story.i_want: to sign in with a username and a password of at least 10 characters and be locked out after repeated failures
user_story.so_that: I can reach the screens for my role while the clinic's accounts stay protected

items.title: Each role sees only what it needs
items.description_md: Every request the system answers is checked against who is asking. A patient reaches only their own data (the patient's family members are added by a later feature, but the rule is built here to cover them). A receptionist reaches only the data of their own clinic. A dentist sees only their own day, read only. The practice manager sees both clinics and the settings. The check uses the signed-in person's role, clinic and active flag read from the database on every request, never ids or roles sent by the browser. Other features use the same check. Searching patients by phone number or name is allowed for receptionists and the manager across all clinics, while appointments stay limited to the receptionist's own clinic. **Why this priority**: This is the security backbone (QA-007). Every later module relies on it, and the PRD makes "a receptionist reaches only their own clinic" a hard requirement. **Independent Test**: With one account of each role, call the same set of protected operations and check each role gets exactly the allowed answers and a refusal otherwise; change a request's clinic id to the other clinic as a receptionist and see it refused; deactivate an account and see its next request refused. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a receptionist of Indiranagar, **When** they ask for the clinic list or for data of Whitefield, **Then** they see Indiranagar only and Whitefield is refused. 2. **Given** a practice manager, **When** they ask for the clinic list, **Then** they see both clinics and the settings screens. 3. **Given** a dentist, **When** they ask for their own day or clinics, **Then** it is allowed read only, and any change request is refused. 4. **Given** a patient, **When** they ask for another patient's data, or send a patient id that is not theirs, **Then** the request is refused; only data owned by the signed-in person is returned. 5. **Given** a signed-in person whose account was just deactivated or whose role changed, **When** they make their next request, **Then** it is refused or handled with the new role at once, without waiting for the session to expire. 6. **Given** any write request from a browser, **When** it lacks the anti-forgery header or comes from another origin, **Then** it is refused. 7. **Given** an unsigned visitor, **When** they call any protected operation, **Then** they get a "sign in" answer and no data. 8. **Given** a receptionist, **When** they search for a patient by phone number or name, **Then** patients of any clinic can be found, but appointments shown with the patient are limited to their own clinic. ---

user_story.as_a: Practice manager (P-04) responsible for patient privacy across both clinics
user_story.i_want: every request to be authorised on the server from the signed-in person's role, clinic and active flag
user_story.so_that: receptionists see only their own clinic, dentists read only, patients reach only their own data, and a deactivated person is locked out at once

items.title: The practice manager manages staff accounts
items.description_md: The practice manager opens the "Staff" screen, creates accounts for receptionists and dentists (name, username, temporary password, role), assigns each receptionist to one clinic, links a dentist account to a dentist record, and deactivates a person who leaves. A deactivated person cannot sign in and any session they hold stops working at once. The manager can also reactivate an account and reset a password. **Why this priority**: Staff accounts are how reception and dentists get in; without this screen only developers could create them. The first manager account is seeded. **Independent Test**: Sign in as the manager, create a receptionist for Whitefield, sign in as that receptionist and see Whitefield only, deactivate them, and see sign-in and the old session refused. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-in manager, **When** they create a receptionist with a username, name, a password of at least 10 characters and a clinic, **Then** the account exists, is active and can sign in. 2. **Given** a signed-in manager, **When** they create a receptionist without a clinic, **Then** the system refuses and says a clinic is required. 3. **Given** a username already in use, **When** the manager creates another account with it, **Then** the system refuses and says the username is taken. 4. **Given** an active staff account that is signed in, **When** the manager deactivates it, **Then** the next request from that person is refused and they cannot sign in again until reactivated. 5. **Given** a receptionist or dentist, **When** they try to create, change or deactivate an account, **Then** the request is refused. 6. **Given** the manager is the only active manager, **When** they try to deactivate themselves, **Then** the system refuses so the practice cannot lock itself out. 7. **Given** a staff member forgot their password, **When** the manager resets it to a new temporary password of at least 10 characters, **Then** the old password stops working and the person's failed-attempt lock is cleared. ---

user_story.i_want: to create, edit, deactivate and reactivate receptionist and dentist accounts, assign receptionists to a clinic and reset passwords
user_story.so_that: staff can get in and leavers are locked out at once without any developer help

Given a username already in use, When the manager creates another account with it, Then the system refuses and says the username is taken
Given an active staff account that is signed in, When the manager deactivates it, Then the next request from that person is refused and they cannot sign in again until reactivated
Given a receptionist or dentist, When they try to create, change or deactivate an account, Then the request is refused
Given the manager is the only active manager, When they try to deactivate themselves, Then the system refuses so the practice cannot lock itself out

Given a staff member forgot their password, When the manager resets it to a new temporary password of at least 10 characters, Then the old password stops working and the person's failed-attempt lock is cleared

items.title: The system holds the clinics and the dentists
items.description_md: The system keeps the clinics (Indiranagar and Whitefield from day one) and the dentists as data. A dentist can work at more than one clinic, on set weekdays. The practice manager adds a third clinic, adds a dentist, and sets which weekdays a dentist works at which clinic, in the staff screens, with no change to the software. Later features give every appointment exactly one clinic and one dentist from these records. **Why this priority**: Every booking, schedule and day view refers to a clinic and a dentist; the third clinic must arrive as data (QA-011). **Independent Test**: On a fresh database both clinics exist; as manager add a third clinic and a dentist who works Monday at Indiranagar and Thursday at Whitefield; the clinic list and dentist list show them, and a deactivated clinic is no longer offered. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a new installation, **When** the clinic list is read, **Then** Indiranagar and Whitefield are present and active. 2. **Given** a signed-in manager, **When** they add a clinic with a name, address and phone number, **Then** it appears in the clinic list at once for all roles that may see it, without a deployment. 3. **Given** a signed-in manager, **When** they add a dentist and set Monday at Indiranagar and Thursday at Whitefield, **Then** the dentist is listed at both clinics, only on those days. 4. **Given** a dentist already has a day at one clinic, **When** the manager assigns the same weekday at a second clinic, **Then** the system refuses, because a dentist is in one place on one day. 5. **Given** a manager deactivates a clinic or a dentist, **When** the lists are read for booking, **Then** the inactive one is not offered, while existing records that point to it stay readable. 6. **Given** a receptionist, **When** they ask to add a clinic or a dentist, **Then** the request is refused. ---

user_story.i_want: to keep clinics and dentists as data, including which weekdays each dentist works at which clinic
user_story.so_that: a third clinic or a new dentist can be added in the staff screens without a software change

items.title: A patient's data is erased on request
items.description_md: When a patient asks (by phone or at reception) to have their data deleted, the practice manager opens an admin screen, finds the patient by phone number, records the request and carries out the erasure. The patient's name, phone number and birth year are anonymised in the person and account records, any open sessions end, and messages held for that person are anonymised too. Appointment rows stay as anonymous counts so that reports are not broken. The screen shows the due date (30 days after the request) and flags overdue requests. **Why this priority**: The privacy requirement (DPDP Act) is mandatory, but it is only needed after real patients exist, so it comes after sign-in and roles; it still ships in Release 1. **Independent Test**: Create a patient account, record an erasure request, run it, and check the name, phone and birth year no longer appear anywhere in the person and account records and the patient cannot sign in with that phone number as the old account. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-in manager and a patient account, **When** the manager records an erasure request, **Then** the request is stored with its date and a due date 30 days later and is listed as open. 2. **Given** an open erasure request, **When** the manager runs the erasure, **Then** the patient's name, phone number and birth year are replaced by anonymous values, their sessions end, and the request is marked done with the date. 3. **Given** an erased patient's former phone number, **When** that number signs in again, **Then** a brand-new account is created after the code is verified; nothing of the old data returns. 4. **Given** an open request that is more than 30 days old, **When** the manager opens the list, **Then** it is flagged as overdue. 5. **Given** a receptionist, dentist or patient, **When** they try to record or run an erasure, **Then** it is refused. 6. **Given** an erasure ran, **When** logs and audit records are read, **Then** they contain the erased person's id only, never name or phone number. ---

user_story.i_want: to record an erasure request, see its 30-day due date and carry out the erasure
user_story.so_that: the patient's name, phone number and birth year are removed within 30 days as the privacy rule requires

items.title: Old identity data is cleaned up automatically
items.description_md: A daily job removes what is no longer needed: sign-in codes after 24 hours, personal data of staff and dentists 24 months after deactivation, and personal data of patient accounts that have not been used for 24 months. The job also provides a place where later features register their own retention rules (appointments 24 months, messages 90 days). **Why this priority**: It keeps the "store only what is needed" promise over time. It is not needed on go-live day, so it can be last, but it is small and built on the same foundation as erasure. **Independent Test**: Insert old records with back-dated times and run the job; old codes disappear, old deactivated staff are anonymised, and recent records are untouched. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a sign-in code created more than 24 hours ago, **When** the daily job runs, **Then** it is deleted. 2. **Given** a staff account deactivated more than 24 months ago, **When** the daily job runs, **Then** its name is anonymised and the account stays deactivated. 3. **Given** a patient account not used for 24 months, **When** the daily job runs, **Then** its personal data is anonymised in the same way as an erasure. 4. **Given** a record inside its retention period, **When** the daily job runs, **Then** it is not changed. 5. **Given** the daily job fails half-way, **When** it is run again, **Then** it finishes the work without double effects. ---

user_story.as_a: Practice manager (P-04) accountable for the clinic's data protection
user_story.i_want: a daily job that deletes old sign-in codes and anonymises long-unused personal data, and lets later features add their own retention rules
user_story.so_that: the system keeps only what it needs, as the privacy rule requires, without manual clean-up

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a sign-in code created more than 24 hours ago, When the daily job runs, Then it is deleted
Given a staff account deactivated more than 24 months ago, When the daily job runs, Then its name is anonymised and the account stays deactivated

Given the daily job fails half-way, When it is run again, Then it finishes the work without double effects

items.title: Manage treatment types
items.description_md: The practice manager opens the treatments screen and sees every treatment type with its duration in minutes and whether patients may book it online. The list starts with the three online types (check-up, cleaning, consultation, 30 minutes each) and reception-only types such as root canal and extraction (60 or 90 minutes). The manager adds a type, changes its name, duration or online flag, and switches a type off when the clinic stops offering it. Booking and slot calculation use this list to know how long a visit lasts and what a patient may book online. **Why this priority**: A slot only has a length once the treatment is known. Free slots (User Story 3) and every booking need this list, so it comes first. **Independent Test**: Sign in as the practice manager, add a 60-minute reception-only type, change a type's duration, switch a type off, then read the list as a patient and as reception. The manager sees all types; a patient sees only active online types. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a new system, **When** the practice manager opens the treatments screen, **Then** the list shows check-up, cleaning and consultation as online, 30 minutes each, and at least root canal and extraction as reception-only with 60 or 90 minutes. 2. **Given** the treatments screen, **When** the manager adds a type with a name, a duration of 30, 60 or 90 minutes and the online flag, **Then** the type is saved and appears in the list at once. 3. **Given** an existing type, **When** the manager changes its duration or online flag, **Then** the change applies to new slot searches and new bookings, and appointments already booked keep their own start and end times. 4. **Given** an active type, **When** the manager switches it off, **Then** it no longer appears for booking, and appointments already booked with it are unchanged. 5. **Given** a type name that already exists (ignoring capital letters), or a duration that is not 30, 60 or 90 minutes, **When** the manager saves, **Then** the save is refused with a message that names the problem. 6. **Given** a signed-in patient, **When** they read the treatment list, **Then** they see only active online types; a receptionist sees all active types. 7. **Given** a user who is not the practice manager, **When** they try to add or change a type, **Then** the request is refused. ---

items.title: Set weekly working hours and breaks
items.description_md: The practice manager opens "dentists and hours", picks a dentist and a clinic and sets, for each weekday, the start and end of the working day and any breaks (for example lunch 13:00–14:00). A dentist can work at more than one clinic on different days. Hours are entered and shown in India time. A dentist with no hours at a clinic offers no slots there. The manager can add a third clinic or dentist later and give them hours in the same screen, with no software release. **Why this priority**: With no hours there are no slots; this is the base of availability. **Independent Test**: As the practice manager, set Dr Rao's Monday hours at Indiranagar to 09:00–17:00 with a break 13:00–14:00, reload and read them back; set Tuesday at Whitefield; try to set Monday at Whitefield overlapping Indiranagar and see it refused. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a dentist and a clinic with no hours, **When** the manager saves Monday 09:00–17:00 with a break 13:00–14:00, **Then** the weekly hours show that day with the break and the same values are returned on reload. 2. **Given** hours for a dentist at one clinic, **When** the manager sets other weekdays at a second clinic, **Then** both sets are kept and shown per clinic. 3. **Given** hours for a weekday, **When** the manager changes the start, end or breaks, **Then** new slot searches use the new hours and appointments already booked are not moved or cancelled. 4. **Given** a weekday entry, **When** the end is not after the start, or a break lies outside the working day or overlaps another break, **Then** the save is refused with a message. 5. **Given** a dentist with hours at clinic A on Monday 09:00–13:00, **When** the manager sets Monday hours at clinic B that overlap 09:00–13:00, **Then** the save is refused because one dentist cannot be at two clinics at once. 6. **Given** a weekday with hours, **When** the manager removes that weekday, **Then** the dentist offers no slots at that clinic on that weekday. 7. **Given** a newly added third clinic and a new dentist (added as data by the staff screens of feature 001), **When** the manager sets their hours, **Then** their slots become available with no software release. 8. **Given** a user who is not the practice manager, **When** they try to change hours, **Then** the request is refused. ---

items.title: Find free slots and first available
items.description_md: Other parts of the system (patient booking, reception booking, rescheduling) ask for free slots of one clinic for one date range and one treatment type, for one dentist or for all that clinic's dentists. A slot is a start time on the hour or half hour at which the whole treatment fits inside the dentist's working hours at that clinic, outside breaks and leave, and not overlapping an appointment already booked. "First available" returns the 10 earliest free slots across the clinic's dentists. Patients see slots only from now to the booking horizon (today plus 30 days, a setting). Slot lists are calculated live so a freed slot is bookable at once. **Why this priority**: This is the module's output; booking (feature 003) cannot start without it. **Independent Test**: With hours 09:00–17:00 and a break 13:00–14:00 for one dentist, one booked appointment 10:00–10:30 and a 30-minute type, ask for one day: slots are 09:00, 09:30, 10:30 … 12:30, 14:00 … 16:30 and nothing at 10:00 or in the break. Ask for a 90-minute type: the last slot is 15:30. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a dentist working 09:00–17:00 with a break 13:00–14:00 at a clinic and no bookings, **When** free slots are requested for a 30-minute type on that day, **Then** slots start every half hour from 09:00 to 16:30 except those inside 13:00–14:00. 2. **Given** a 60-minute or 90-minute type, **When** free slots are requested, **Then** only starts where the full duration fits before the end of the day and before the next break, leave or booked appointment are returned (for example 12:30 is not offered for 60 minutes when the break starts at 13:00). 3. **Given** a booked appointment 10:00–10:30, **When** free slots are requested, **Then** the 10:00 slot is not offered, and a 60-minute type is not offered at 09:30 or 10:00. 4. **Given** leave covering part of the day, **When** free slots are requested, **Then** no slot overlaps the leave. 5. **Given** an appointment is cancelled, **When** free slots are requested again, **Then** its slot appears at once. 6. **Given** a patient asks for slots, **When** the range goes past today plus the booking horizon (30 days) or starts in the past, **Then** only slots from now to the horizon are returned (1 March shows up to 31 March). 7. **Given** a clinic with several dentists, **When** "first available" is requested for a treatment type, **Then** the 10 earliest free slots across those dentists are returned in time order, each with its dentist. 8. **Given** a treatment type that is not bookable online, **When** a patient asks for its slots, **Then** the request is refused; a receptionist or manager can ask for it. 9. **Given** a receptionist of clinic A, **When** they ask for slots of clinic B, **Then** the request is refused. 10. **Given** 3 clinics, 10 dentists and 1,000 appointments a week, **When** 100 users ask for free slots at the same time, **Then** 95% of the answers come back fast enough for the slot list to show within 2 seconds on a 4G phone. 11. **Given** a request with a date range longer than 31 days, **When** slots are asked, **Then** the request is refused with a message. ---

items.title: Record dentist leave and list appointments to move
items.description_md: The practice manager opens the leave screen, picks a dentist and records leave for whole days or for part of a day (for example Thursday 14:00–17:00). Free slots stop being offered in that time at every clinic where the dentist works. If appointments are already booked in that time, the system lists them (patient, phone, clinic, treatment, time) so reception can phone the patients and move them. The system never moves or cancels an appointment itself, including those that conflict with leave added after booking. The manager can change or delete leave. **Why this priority**: Without leave, slots would be offered while the dentist is away; the "to move" list protects patients already booked. It needs hours (User Story 2) and the slot calculation (User Story 3) to be seen in action. **Independent Test**: Book an appointment for Dr Rao on Thursday 15:00, record leave Thursday 14:00–17:00, check that the appointment is listed as "to move", that it is still booked and unchanged, and that no slot is offered 14:00–17:00. Delete the leave and see the slots return. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a dentist with hours, **When** the manager records whole-day leave for a date range, **Then** no free slots are offered for that dentist on those days at any clinic. 2. **Given** a dentist, **When** the manager records part-day leave from 14:00 to 17:00, **Then** slots in that time are not offered and slots before and after are. 3. **Given** appointments already booked in the leave time, **When** the leave is saved, **Then** those appointments are listed with patient name, phone number, clinic, treatment and start time, and each stays booked and unchanged. 4. **Given** a leave with a "to move" list, **When** reception moves or cancels one of those appointments and the list is opened again, **Then** that appointment is no longer on it. 5. **Given** a receptionist of clinic A, **When** they open the list, **Then** they see only appointments at clinic A; the manager sees all clinics. 6. **Given** leave, **When** the manager changes its dates or times, **Then** the list and the slots follow the new times; when the manager deletes it, the slots in that time are offered again. 7. **Given** a leave whose end is not after its start, or that overlaps another leave of the same dentist, **When** the manager saves, **Then** the save is refused with a message. 8. **Given** leave that ended more than 24 months ago, **When** the yearly clean-up runs, **Then** it is deleted; newer leave stays. 9. **Given** a user who is not the practice manager, **When** they try to record leave, **Then** the request is refused. ---

items.title: Online booking by patients (MOD-03)
items.description_md: Patient books clinic, online treatment, dentist or first available, free slot within 30 days; no double booking. RELEASE 1 (DL-1, due 2027-02-22, hard). PRD ids: FR-011, FR-012.
open_questions: ESTIMATE CHECK (scope/estimate.md, 1 SP = 6 h, 8 h per person-day): E-003 = 35 SP = 210 h = 26.25 pd against MOD-03 9-14 pd (1.9-2.9x the range; above the high end). Includes two load/performance proof stories (S-003-US4, S-003-US5; 6 SP) for NFR-001/NFR-002, which estimate.md does not list separately. Flag: re-baseline or cut scope (decision for the Delivery Manager).

items.title: Find a free slot
items.description_md: A signed-in patient opens "Book", chooses the clinic and one of the online treatment types (check-up, cleaning, consultation), then chooses a dentist at that clinic or "first available", and sees the free slots for a day within the next 30 days. With "first available" the patient sees the earliest free slots across all of that clinic's dentists. **Why this priority**: Without seeing real free slots, no booking is possible. It is the first half of the core flow. **Independent Test**: Sign in as a patient, pick a clinic, a treatment and "first available", and check that the 10 earliest free slots are shown in time order, each with its dentist. Pick a named dentist and a day and check that only that dentist's free slots are shown. Check that day 31 and later are not offered. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-in patient on the "who and what" screen, **When** they open the treatment list for a clinic, **Then** only online-bookable treatment types (check-up, cleaning, consultation) are offered, and reception-only types are not. 2. **Given** a clinic with several dentists who have free slots, **When** the patient chooses "first available", **Then** the system shows the earliest free slots across that clinic's dentists (at most 10, earliest first), each with dentist name, date and time. 3. **Given** a patient who chose a named dentist, **When** they pick a day, **Then** the free slots of that dentist for that day are shown, on the hour or half hour. 4. **Given** today is 1 March, **When** the patient looks at days, **Then** days from 1 March up to and including 31 March can be chosen and later days cannot (the window is today plus 30 days, a setting). 5. **Given** a day with no free slots, **When** the patient picks it, **Then** the screen says no slots are free that day and suggests the next day that has free slots. 6. **Given** a patient who is not signed in, **When** they ask for slots, **Then** they are sent to sign in first (feature 001) and return to the same choice afterwards. ---

user_story.i_want: to choose a clinic, an online treatment and a dentist or "first available" and see the free slots in the next 30 days
user_story.so_that: I can pick a time that suits me without phoning the clinic

items.title: Confirm and see the booking
items.description_md: After picking a slot, the patient chooses SMS or WhatsApp for messages about this visit, reviews a summary (who, clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time, channel) and confirms. The system books the appointment for the patient's own account and shows the "booked" screen with the details. A confirmation message is requested and delivered shortly after (feature 006), not while the patient waits. **Why this priority**: It completes the core flow and creates the appointment record that every later feature uses. **Independent Test**: As a signed-in patient pick a free slot, choose a channel, confirm; check that the appointment exists with status "booked" for that patient, that exactly one "booked" history entry exists with who and when, that the "booked" screen shows clinic, dentist, treatment, date and time, and that a confirmation message was queued. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient who picked a free slot, **When** they choose SMS or WhatsApp and confirm, **Then** the appointment is saved with status "booked" for their own account and the "booked" screen shows clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time and the chosen channel. 2. **Given** a first-time booker, **When** the confirm screen opens, **Then** SMS is pre-selected as the default channel. 3. **Given** a successful booking, **When** it is saved, **Then** one history entry "booked" with the patient as actor and the time is saved together with it, and a confirmation message request and the reminder record are saved in the same step. 4. **Given** a successful booking, **When** the messaging provider is slow or down, **Then** the patient still sees the "booked" screen and the booking stays. 5. **Given** the patient taps "Confirm" twice or their phone retries the request (same booking attempt), **When** the system receives both, **Then** only one appointment exists and both answers show that same appointment. 6. **Given** a request that names another patient's account, **When** a patient submits it, **Then** it is refused and nothing is booked (a patient books only for their own account). 7. **Given** the "is this patient blocked" check, **When** a booking is made in Release 1, **Then** the check always allows booking (the real block arrives in Release 2). 8. **Given** a slow network, **When** no answer arrives within 10 seconds, **Then** the patient is told the result is unknown and is offered to check their appointments before trying again; the booking is never retried automatically. ---

items.title: A slot is never booked twice
items.description_md: If another booking takes the slot while the patient is choosing, the patient is told "this slot was just taken" and is shown the next free slots (same clinic, treatment and dentist choice) to pick again, without starting over. **Why this priority**: Double-booking is the one failure reception cannot accept; it is an architecture driver. **Independent Test**: Two patients confirm the same slot at the same moment; exactly one booking succeeds, the other gets the "slot taken" message with next free slots, and only one active appointment exists for that dentist and time. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** two patients who confirm the same free slot at the same time, **When** both requests are processed, **Then** exactly one appointment is created and the other patient is told the slot was just taken. 2. **Given** a patient told the slot was taken, **When** the message appears, **Then** the next free slots for the same clinic, treatment and dentist choice are shown on the same screen and the patient can pick one and confirm. 3. **Given** a slot taken after "first available", **When** the patient is shown next free slots, **Then** they come from across the clinic's dentists again (at most 10). 4. **Given** a slot that overlaps part of another active appointment of the same dentist, **When** a booking is attempted, **Then** it is refused in the same way, not only when start times are equal. 5. **Given** a cancelled appointment, **When** another patient books its slot, **Then** the booking succeeds (only active appointments block a slot). 6. **Given** a slot that is no longer free for a reason other than a booking (for example, leave was added), **When** the patient confirms, **Then** the patient gets the same "slot no longer available" message with next free slots. ---

user_story.i_want: to be told when someone else takes my slot and to see the next free slots straight away
user_story.so_that: I can pick again without starting over and am never double-booked

items.title: Prove no double booking under load
items.description_md: A test story: an automated concurrency test attacks the same slots with many simultaneous booking attempts and proves that no two active appointments ever overlap for one dentist. **Why this priority**: The 0-overlap guarantee is a headline quality target; it has to be shown, not assumed. **Independent Test**: Run the concurrency suite: 1,000 runs, each with simultaneous attempts on the same dentist and slot (and on overlapping slots); after each run count active overlapping appointments. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a free slot and at least 30 simultaneous booking attempts for it, **When** a run finishes, **Then** exactly one attempt succeeded, all others got "slot taken", and 0 overlapping active appointments exist. 2. **Given** 1,000 such runs, **When** all finish, **Then** 0 overlapping active appointments were found in 100% of runs. 3. **Given** the same booking attempt sent several times at once with the same retry key, **When** the run finishes, **Then** exactly one appointment exists. 4. **Given** the test report, **When** reviewed, **Then** it lists the number of runs, attempts, successes, conflicts and overlaps found. ---

user_story.as_a: practice manager (P-04) accountable for the clinics
user_story.i_want: automated proof that no two active appointments ever overlap for one dentist under simultaneous booking attempts
user_story.so_that: reception never has to resolve a double booking at go-live

items.title: Prove booking speed on a phone network
items.description_md: A test story: a load test with realistic phone-network conditions measures how fast free slots appear and how fast a booking is confirmed. **Why this priority**: The speed targets are customer-visible and must be verified before go-live. **Independent Test**: Run the load test with 100 concurrent simulated patients on a 4G network profile; read the 95th-percentile timings for slot lists and for booking confirmation. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** 100 concurrent simulated patients on a 4G profile, **When** they open the slot picker, **Then** free slots are shown within 2 seconds for 95% of requests (server share at most 500 ms at the 95th percentile). 2. **Given** the same load, **When** patients confirm bookings, **Then** the confirmation is shown within 3 seconds for 95% of requests (server share at most 800 ms at the 95th percentile). 3. **Given** the "first available" view for a clinic with all dentists, **When** it is requested under load, **Then** it returns at most 10 slots and meets scenario 1. 4. **Given** the test report, **When** reviewed, **Then** it states pass or fail against these limits and the data volume used (at least a year of appointments for 3 clinics and 10 dentists). ---

items.title: Booking works on a phone for a new patient
items.description_md: A mobile usability acceptance story: a new patient completes a booking on an Android or iPhone in no more than 5 screens after sign-in, with large tap targets and no sideways scrolling. **Why this priority**: Patients of all ages use phones; the screens must work without help. **Independent Test**: Run the booking flow on current Chrome and Safari on an Android phone and an iPhone (or their emulators): count screens after sign-in, measure tap target size, check for sideways scrolling at 320, 360 and 390 px widths. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a new patient who has just signed in, **When** they book a visit, **Then** they reach the "booked" screen after 5 screens or fewer (who and what, slot picker, confirm, booked). 2. **Given** every patient screen in this flow, **When** viewed on current Chrome and Safari on Android and iPhone at widths from 320 px, **Then** there is no sideways scrolling. 3. **Given** every button, link, slot and field in this flow, **When** measured, **Then** each tap target is at least 44 px high and wide. 4. **Given** "Back" is used on the phone, **When** the patient returns from a later screen, **Then** their earlier choices are still filled in. 5. **Given** all texts and times in the flow, **When** viewed, **Then** they are in English and times are in India time (IST). ---

items.title: See my appointments
items.description_md: A signed-in patient opens "My appointments" and sees their upcoming appointments and their past appointments, each with clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time (India time) and status. Choosing one opens the appointment screen with the full details. The list is built per person of the account, so when family members arrive in Release 2 their appointments appear in their own group with no change to the screen; in Release 1 only the account holder's own appointments are listed. On the appointment screen the patient sees "Change time" and "Cancel" buttons when the change is still allowed, or the clinic's phone number when it is not. **Why this priority**: Every other story starts here, and it is useful by itself: patients can check a booking without phoning reception. **Independent Test**: Sign in as a patient with two upcoming, one past and one cancelled appointment, open "My appointments", and check grouping, status text, IST times and that another patient's appointments never appear. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-in patient with upcoming and past appointments, **When** they open "My appointments", **Then** they see the upcoming ones first (earliest first) and the past ones below (latest first), each with clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time in IST and status. 2. **Given** a patient with a cancelled appointment and an appointment marked arrived or no-show, **When** they open "My appointments", **Then** those appear in the past group with the status shown in plain words (for example "Cancelled by you", "Cancelled by the clinic", "Attended", "Missed"). 3. **Given** a patient with no appointments, **When** they open "My appointments", **Then** they see a short message and a "Book" button. 4. **Given** a signed-in patient, **When** they ask for the appointment of another patient (by changing the id in the address), **Then** the system answers as if it does not exist and shows no data of that other patient. 5. **Given** an upcoming appointment that starts in more than 4 hours, **When** the patient opens it, **Then** the buttons "Change time" and "Cancel" are shown. **Given** one that starts in 4 hours or less, **When** the patient opens it, **Then** the buttons are replaced by the clinic's phone number. 6. **Given** a phone with a narrow screen, **When** the patient uses these screens, **Then** nothing needs sideways scrolling and every button is easy to tap. ---

items.title: Cancel an upcoming appointment
items.description_md: A patient opens an upcoming appointment, chooses "Cancel", confirms, and sees a "Done" screen saying the appointment is cancelled. The slot is free at once for other patients, the appointment's reminder is withdrawn, and the patient gets a message in the channel they chose for that appointment. Cancelling is possible until 4 hours before the start; after that the page shows the clinic's phone number instead of the buttons and the system refuses a cancel sent by other means. **Why this priority**: It frees chairs for other patients, which is the point of the product, and it is the simplest of the two changes. **Independent Test**: Cancel an appointment 5 hours ahead and check status, free slot, history row and message; then try an appointment 3 hours ahead and check that no cancel is possible. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an upcoming appointment more than 4 hours away, **When** the patient chooses "Cancel" and confirms, **Then** the appointment status becomes "cancelled by the patient", the "Done" screen shows the result, and a record of who cancelled and when is kept. 2. **Given** a cancelled appointment, **When** another patient looks for slots of that dentist at that time, **Then** the slot is offered at once and can be booked. 3. **Given** a cancelled appointment, **When** the cancel is done, **Then** the patient gets a message in the channel chosen for that appointment stating clinic, dentist, date and time of the cancelled visit, and no reminder is sent for it. 4. **Given** an appointment 4 hours or less away, **When** the patient opens it, **Then** no "Cancel" button is shown, the clinic phone number is shown, and a cancel request made some other way is refused with the same phone number in the answer. 5. **Given** the patient chooses "Cancel", **When** they do not confirm (they go back), **Then** nothing changes. 6. **Given** the patient taps "Confirm" twice, **When** the second request arrives, **Then** the appointment is cancelled once, one message is sent, and the patient sees the same "Done" screen. 7. **Given** the message provider is unavailable, **When** the patient cancels, **Then** the cancel still succeeds and the message is sent later. ---

user_story.i_want: to cancel it myself with a confirmation until 4 hours before the start
user_story.so_that: the slot is freed for others at once and I get a message in my chosen channel without phoning reception

items.title: Reschedule an upcoming appointment
items.description_md: A patient opens an upcoming appointment, chooses "Change time", and sees free slots for the same clinic and the same treatment with any dentist. They pick one, confirm, and see a "Done" screen with the new time. The old slot becomes free at once, the reminder moves to the new time, and the patient gets a message in their chosen channel. Rescheduling is possible until 4 hours before the current start. If someone else takes the chosen slot first, the patient is told and shown the next free slots. A later rule (feature 006, FR-025) may block rescheduling; this feature calls a policy check that always allows it in Release 1. **Why this priority**: Important to keep patients instead of losing them to a cancel, but it builds on the screens and rules of the first two stories. **Independent Test**: Reschedule an appointment 2 days ahead to a free slot with another dentist; check new time, freed old slot, history row, message; then race two patients for one slot and check one wins. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an upcoming appointment more than 4 hours away, **When** the patient chooses "Change time", **Then** they see free slots for the same clinic and treatment from any dentist, within the same booking horizon as new bookings, never the slot they already hold. 2. **Given** the patient picks a free slot and confirms, **When** the change is saved, **Then** the appointment has the new date, time and dentist, keeps its clinic, treatment and channel, and the "Done" screen shows the new details. 3. **Given** the change is saved, **When** another patient looks for slots, **Then** the old slot is offered at once. 4. **Given** the change is saved, **When** messages are created, **Then** the patient gets a message in the channel chosen for that appointment with the new clinic, dentist, date and time, and the old reminder is withdrawn so that only a reminder for the new time can exist. 5. **Given** another patient takes the chosen slot while this patient is choosing, **When** the patient confirms, **Then** nothing changes, the patient is told the slot was just taken and is shown the next free slots, and keeps their original appointment. 6. **Given** an appointment 4 hours or less away, **When** the patient opens it, **Then** no "Change time" button is shown, the clinic phone number is shown, and a change request made some other way is refused. 7. **Given** the no-show policy says a patient may not reschedule, **When** the patient chooses "Change time", **Then** the page shows the clinic phone number instead. In Release 1 the policy always allows. 8. **Given** a reschedule, **When** the history is read, **Then** it shows who changed the appointment, when, and the old and new time. ---

user_story.as_a: patient (P-01) who cannot make my appointment time
user_story.i_want: to move it to another free slot of the same clinic and treatment until 4 hours before
user_story.so_that: I keep my visit instead of cancelling, the old slot is freed at once and I get a message in my chosen channel

items.title: Open an appointment from a message link
items.description_md: A patient taps the link in a confirmation, change message or reminder. If they are signed in, the appointment screen opens at once. If not, they sign in with their phone code and then land on that same appointment. A link only opens an appointment of the signed-in patient; for anyone else it behaves as an unknown appointment. This lets the patient reach "Change time" or "Cancel" in one tap from the reminder. **Why this priority**: It turns the reminder into a one-tap way to free a slot, but the stories above work without it through "My appointments". **Independent Test**: Open the link of an appointment in a fresh browser, sign in, and check that the appointment screen opens; repeat with another patient's account and check that it does not. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient who is not signed in, **When** they open the appointment link, **Then** they are asked to sign in and, after signing in, the appointment screen opens. 2. **Given** a signed-in patient, **When** they open the link of their own appointment, **Then** the appointment screen opens at once with the buttons or the phone number according to the 4-hour rule. 3. **Given** a patient signed in as someone else, **When** they open the link, **Then** they see "appointment not found" and no data of the appointment. 4. **Given** a link to a cancelled or past appointment, **When** the patient opens it, **Then** the appointment screen shows its status without buttons. ---

user_story.i_want: the link in the message to open my appointment after I sign in
user_story.so_that: I can change or cancel in one tap, and nobody else can open it

items.title: Reception sees the day of their clinic
items.description_md: A receptionist signs in at the desk PC and lands on today's day view of their own clinic: one column per dentist who works there that day, and in each column the appointments in time order with patient name, phone number, treatment and status. They can move to the previous or next day, or pick a date, and see that day the same way. They never see appointments of another clinic. **Why this priority**: Every other reception action (arrive, no-show, book, move, cancel) starts from this screen. Without it reception cannot run the day, and it replaces the paper diary per dentist. **Independent Test**: Seed one clinic with three dentists working today (one also working at another clinic on another day) and appointments in several statuses. Sign in as that clinic's receptionist, open the day view, step to tomorrow and back, and check the columns, the fields and that the other clinic's appointments are absent. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a receptionist of clinic A is signed in and three dentists work at clinic A today, **When** they open the day view, **Then** today's date in India time is shown with exactly three columns, one per dentist, each listing that dentist's appointments in time order. 2. **Given** an appointment exists, **When** it appears in the day view, **Then** it shows patient name, phone number, treatment and status, and the status is one of booked, arrived, no-show, cancelled by the patient or cancelled by the clinic. 3. **Given** a dentist has no working hours at clinic A on the chosen day, **When** the receptionist views that day, **Then** that dentist has no column. 4. **Given** the day view of today, **When** the receptionist moves to the next day, the previous day or a chosen date, **Then** the columns and appointments of that day are shown. 5. **Given** appointments exist at clinic B, **When** the receptionist of clinic A opens any day or asks for a clinic B appointment directly, **Then** none of clinic B's appointments are shown and a direct request is refused. ---

user_story.so_that: I can see every dentist's day at a glance and run the desk without the paper diary

items.title: Reception marks arrived and no-show, and can undo
items.description_md: When a patient reaches the desk the receptionist marks the appointment as arrived. When a patient has not come, the receptionist marks the appointment as a no-show, which is allowed from 15 minutes after the start time until the end of that day (India time). A no-show can be undone on the same day, which puts the appointment back to booked. Every status change records who made it and when, so a later question ("who marked this?") has an answer. **Why this priority**: This is the core of the no-show goal (REQ-002): the no-show data that the block (R2) and the monthly report (R2) count is created here. **Independent Test**: Create booked appointments starting 5, 20 and 120 minutes ago and one tomorrow. As receptionist mark the first arrived, try a no-show on the first (refused, it is arrived) and on the 5-minute one before and after the 15-minute mark, mark the 20-minute one as no-show then undo it, and read the history of each appointment. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a booked appointment of the receptionist's clinic, **When** the receptionist marks the patient as arrived, **Then** the status becomes arrived and the day view shows it. 2. **Given** a booked appointment that started 15 minutes ago or more today, **When** the receptionist marks a no-show, **Then** the status becomes no-show. 3. **Given** a booked appointment that started less than 15 minutes ago, or has not started yet, **When** the receptionist tries to mark a no-show, **Then** the request is refused with a message that says from which time it is allowed, and the status stays booked. 4. **Given** an appointment on an earlier day that is still booked, **When** the receptionist tries to mark a no-show, **Then** the request is refused because the day has ended. 5. **Given** an appointment marked no-show today, **When** the receptionist undoes it the same day, **Then** the status returns to booked; **and when** the day has ended, **Then** undo is refused. 6. **Given** any status change (arrived, no-show, undo, cancel), **When** it is made, **Then** the change is stored with the previous and new status, the staff member who made it and the time, and that history can be read for the appointment. 7. **Given** an appointment that is arrived, no-show or cancelled, **When** a change is attempted that the status rules do not allow (for example marking an arrived patient a no-show, or arriving a cancelled appointment), **Then** it is refused and nothing is changed. 8. **Given** two receptionists act on the same appointment at the same time, **When** both save, **Then** one change is kept, the other is told the appointment was changed and sees the current status. ---

user_story.i_want: to mark a patient arrived, mark a no-show from 15 minutes after the start until the end of the day, and undo it that day
user_story.so_that: no-show data is correct and every status change shows who made it and when

items.title: Reception finds or creates a patient
items.description_md: When a patient phones or walks in, the receptionist searches for them by phone number or by name. If the patient is found the receptionist selects them; if not, the receptionist creates the patient with a name and a phone number. Patients are not tied to one clinic, so the search covers all patients, but selecting a patient never shows appointments of another clinic. **Why this priority**: Booking for callers and walk-ins (User Story 4) needs a patient first, and this is the first step of the "patient phones or walks in" flow. **Independent Test**: Seed patients, one with the same name as another and one booked mainly at the other clinic. As receptionist search by full phone number, by part of a phone number, and by name; create a new patient with name and phone; try to create one with an existing phone number. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** patients exist, **When** the receptionist enters a phone number or part of one (at least 4 digits), **Then** the matching patients are listed with name and phone number. 2. **Given** patients exist, **When** the receptionist enters part of a name (at least 2 letters), **Then** the matching patients are listed with name and phone number, ordered by best match. 3. **Given** a patient who has only booked at the other clinic, **When** the receptionist searches for them, **Then** they are found, and no appointment of the other clinic is shown. 4. **Given** no patient matches, **When** the receptionist enters a name and a phone number and saves, **Then** a patient is created and selected for booking. 5. **Given** a phone number that already belongs to a patient account, **When** the receptionist tries to create a patient with that phone number, **Then** the existing patient is offered instead of a duplicate. 6. **Given** a missing name, or a phone number that is not a valid Indian mobile number, **When** the receptionist saves, **Then** the form shows what must be corrected and nothing is created. ---

user_story.i_want: to find a patient by phone number or name, or create one with name and phone number
user_story.so_that: I can book phone callers and walk-ins quickly without creating duplicates

items.title: Reception books, moves and cancels for patients
items.description_md: For the selected patient the receptionist books any treatment type, including the reception-only 60 and 90 minute types, with a dentist of their clinic in a free slot. This also covers a walk-in: the patient is booked into a free slot and marked arrived straight away. The receptionist can move an appointment to another free slot (or another dentist) and cancel an appointment. None of this has the 4-hour cut-off that applies to patients online. When cancelling, the receptionist says whether the patient asked (status "cancelled by the patient") or the clinic cancelled (status "cancelled by the clinic"). Future appointments from the paper diary are typed in this way before go-live, with no import. **Why this priority**: Phone and walk-in booking is how most appointments are made on go-live day, and reception-only treatments can be booked nowhere else. **Independent Test**: As receptionist, book a patient for a 90-minute reception-only treatment in a free slot 1 hour from now, book a walk-in into the current slot and see it arrived, move the first appointment to another dentist, try to book an overlapping slot, cancel one as "patient asked" and one as "clinic cancelled", and check statuses, the day view and the history. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a selected patient, **When** the receptionist picks any active treatment type (online or reception-only), a dentist of their clinic and a free slot and confirms, **Then** the appointment is booked in the clinic for that dentist and appears at once in the day view. 2. **Given** a slot starts in less than 4 hours, **When** the receptionist books, moves or cancels an appointment in it, **Then** the action is allowed, because reception has no 4-hour cut-off. 3. **Given** a patient who walks in, **When** the receptionist books a free slot and chooses "walk-in", **Then** a normal appointment is created with status arrived and it counts like any other appointment. 4. **Given** the slot is taken by another booking while the receptionist is choosing, **When** they confirm, **Then** nothing is double booked, they are told the slot is taken and are shown the next free slots. 5. **Given** a booked appointment, **When** the receptionist moves it to another free slot of the same or another dentist at their clinic, **Then** the old slot is free at once, the appointment keeps its patient and treatment, and the move is recorded in the history. 6. **Given** a booked appointment, **When** the receptionist cancels it and states that the patient asked, **Then** the status becomes cancelled by the patient; **and when** the clinic cancelled, **Then** the status becomes cancelled by the clinic. In both cases the slot is free at once. 7. **Given** a booking, move or cancel by reception, **When** it is saved, **Then** the patient gets the confirmation or change message in their channel, as delivered by the messages feature (006); a failure to send does not undo the booking. 8. **Given** the appointment belongs to the other clinic, **When** the receptionist tries to move or cancel it, **Then** it is refused. 9. **Given** a typed-in future appointment before go-live (paper diary), **When** the receptionist books it, **Then** it works the same as any booking, so the dry run in the week before go-live can use these screens. ---

items.title: Dentist sees their own day, read only
items.description_md: A dentist signs in on a phone or the clinic PC and sees today's appointments at each clinic where they work today: time, patient name, treatment and status. The screen is read only: no arrive, no-show, book, move or cancel. The dentist can move to other days. Sign in as the first dentist and check that both clinics are shown with only their own appointments, that no action is offered, and that action requests are refused. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a dentist works at clinic A in the morning and clinic B in the afternoon today, **When** they open "my day", **Then** the appointments of both clinics are shown, grouped by clinic, in time order. 2. **Given** an appointment, **When** it is shown, **Then** it has time, patient name, treatment and status, and no change action is offered. 3. **Given** a dentist signed in, **When** they try to change an appointment or to read another dentist's day, **Then** the request is refused. 4. **Given** a phone-sized screen, **When** the dentist opens "my day", **Then** it is readable without sideways scrolling. ---

items.title: Confirmations, reminders and opt-out via SMS and WhatsApp
items.description_md: Channel choice, booking confirmation, 24-hour reminder with quiet hours, skip rules, reminder content with link, STOP opt-out, DLT/template compliance. RELEASE 1 (DL-1, due 2027-02-22, hard). PRD ids: FR-013, FR-014, FR-027, FR-028, FR-030, FR-031.
open_questions: Q-009 (night-time reminder time) is open: the spec uses the default SA-003/PD-004 (quiet hours 21:00-08:00, 20:00 evening send, 08:00 fallback). Quiet hours, 20:00 and 08:00 are configuration values so a different answer needs no code change.

SMS and WhatsApp providers are not selected (ASM-009): sandbox adapters only; real adapters (T021, T022, receipt/STOP parsers, signatures) must be re-checked against the chosen providers' real API and assume receipt webhooks, STOP forwarding and a test account in weeks 1-2.

DLT sender ID/template registration (DEP-001) and WhatsApp template approval (DEP-002) are done by the clinic with our help (A-005); late approval (RSK-001) is the main schedule risk for the 2027-02-22 UAT date.

The spec reads STOP from the SMS channel only (the WhatsApp webhook carries receipts, not inbound text). A WhatsApp-only patient can stop reminders via reception or by replying STOP to an SMS. Does NFR-011 / FR-031 ('replying STOP') accept this? To confirm with the client.

ESTIMATE CHECK (scope/estimate.md, 1 SP = 6 h, 8 h per person-day): E-006 = 42 SP = 252 h = 31.5 pd against MOD-07 15-24 pd (1.3-2.1x the range; above the high end). MOD-07 in estimate.md also covers the fallback and failed list (now E-009, 23 SP = 17.25 pd): E-006 + E-009 = 65 SP = 48.75 pd against 15-24 pd (2.0-3.25x). LARGE GAP: re-baseline or cut scope (decision for the Delivery Manager).

items.title: Choose SMS or WhatsApp when booking
items.description_md: On the confirm screen of the booking flow the patient picks SMS or WhatsApp for messages about this appointment. SMS is pre-selected the first time. Whatever they pick is pre-selected next time they book. **Why this priority**: Every message in this feature goes to the channel the patient chose; without the choice nothing can be sent. It is also the only patient-visible screen change of the feature. **Independent Test**: Book once choosing WhatsApp, start a second booking and see WhatsApp pre-selected; a brand-new patient sees SMS pre-selected. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient who has never booked, **When** they reach the confirm screen, **Then** SMS is pre-selected and WhatsApp can be chosen instead. 2. **Given** a patient who chose WhatsApp on their last booking, **When** they reach the confirm screen of a new booking, **Then** WhatsApp is pre-selected. 3. **Given** a patient who confirms a booking with a channel, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** the appointment records that channel and it becomes the patient's remembered choice. 4. **Given** a patient who chose WhatsApp for an appointment, **When** messages about it are sent, **Then** they go only to WhatsApp, never to both channels. ---

user_story.i_want: to choose SMS or WhatsApp on the confirm screen and have my last choice pre-selected next time
user_story.so_that: I receive messages about my appointment in the channel I actually use

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a patient who has never booked, When they reach the confirm screen, Then SMS is pre-selected and WhatsApp can be chosen instead
Given a patient who chose WhatsApp on their last booking, When they reach the confirm screen of a new booking, Then WhatsApp is pre-selected
Given a patient who confirms a booking with a channel, When the booking is saved, Then the appointment records that channel and it becomes the patient's remembered choice
Given a patient who chose WhatsApp for an appointment, When messages about it are sent, Then they go only to WhatsApp, never to both channels

dependencies.reason: user stories start after foundational work
Channel choice is part of the booking confirmation step

estimate.rationale: 6 tasks (~18 h): one GET endpoint, a channel field on the booking request, a small radio-group component and its wiring; coordination with the booking feature is the only unknown.

items.title: Immediate booking confirmation
items.description_md: Right after a booking is saved the patient receives a confirmation in the chosen channel: clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time (India time) and a link to the appointment. The booking screen does not wait for the message to be delivered. **Why this priority**: The confirmation is the first proof to the patient that the booking exists; it also exercises the whole sending path (templates, providers, status) that the reminder story reuses. **Independent Test**: Book an appointment against the sandbox providers; within 1 minute a confirmation with the five details and a working link is recorded as sent in the chosen channel. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient confirms a booking with SMS, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** a confirmation SMS is sent within 1 minute giving clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time in IST and a link to the appointment. 2. **Given** a patient confirms a booking with WhatsApp, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** the confirmation is sent as an approved WhatsApp template message with the same details. 3. **Given** the booking fails (for example the slot was just taken), **When** the patient sees the "slot taken" answer, **Then** no confirmation is sent. 4. **Given** the provider is down when the booking is saved, **When** the patient confirms, **Then** the booking still succeeds and the confirmation stays queued and is retried. 5. **Given** a patient who has switched reminders off, **When** they book, **Then** the confirmation is still sent. ---

user_story.i_want: to get a confirmation in my chosen channel with clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time and a link
user_story.so_that: I know my booking exists and can open it

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a patient confirms a booking with SMS, When the booking is saved, Then a confirmation SMS is sent within 1 minute giving clinic, dentist, treatment, date, time in IST and a link to the appointment
Given a patient confirms a booking with WhatsApp, When the booking is saved, Then the confirmation is sent as an approved WhatsApp template message with the same details
Given the booking fails (for example the slot was just taken), When the patient sees the "slot taken" answer, Then no confirmation is sent
Given the provider is down when the booking is saved, When the patient confirms, Then the booking still succeeds and the confirmation stays queued and is retried
Given a patient who has switched reminders off, When they book, Then the confirmation is still sent

open_questions: SMS and WhatsApp providers are not selected (ASM-009): the real SMS and WhatsApp adapters (T021, T022) can only be finished against a chosen provider's API; estimate assumes a standard template-send HTTP API.
DLT sender/template registration (DEP-001) and WhatsApp template approval (DEP-002) must be done before real confirmations can go out in production (RSK-001); sandbox providers are used until then.
The confirmation link points to the appointment page of feature 004; the link format and sign-in deep link need agreeing with E-004.

items.title: Reminder 24 hours before, with quiet hours
items.description_md: Twenty-four hours before the appointment the patient receives a reminder in the chosen channel stating clinic, dentist, date and time (IST) and a link to reschedule or cancel. A reminder that would fall due between 21:00 and 08:00 India time is sent at 20:00 the evening before the quiet period; if that time has already passed when the booking is made, it is sent at once when outside quiet hours, otherwise at 08:00. **Why this priority**: Reducing no-shows is the main goal of the product (goal REQ-002); this is the feature that delivers it. **Independent Test**: Create bookings at fixed times in a test clock (due at 14:00, due at 22:30, due at 03:00, booked 30 hours ahead for a night-time due, booked 10 hours ahead) and check the scheduled send time of each reminder and that it is sent within 15 minutes of that time. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an appointment tomorrow at 14:00 booked a week ago, **When** the due time (today 14:00) arrives, **Then** the reminder is sent within 15 minutes in the chosen channel with clinic, dentist, date, time (IST) and a link to reschedule or cancel. 2. **Given** an appointment whose reminder is due at 22:30 IST, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** the reminder is scheduled for 20:00 IST the same evening. 3. **Given** an appointment whose reminder is due at 03:00 IST, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** the reminder is scheduled for 20:00 IST the evening before the due time. 4. **Given** a reminder whose adjusted 20:00 time has already passed when the booking is made, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** the reminder goes at once if it is outside 21:00-08:00 IST, otherwise at 08:00 IST. 5. **Given** an appointment booked less than 24 hours before it starts, **When** the booking is saved, **Then** no reminder is created and only the confirmation is sent. 6. **Given** the reminder link, **When** the patient opens it, **Then** it opens that appointment where they can reschedule or cancel. ---

user_story.i_want: to get one reminder 24 hours before, not in the night, with a link to reschedule or cancel
user_story.so_that: I remember the appointment or change it in time, which reduces no-shows

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an appointment tomorrow at 14:00 booked a week ago, When the due time (today 14:00) arrives, Then the reminder is sent within 15 minutes in the chosen channel with clinic, dentist, date, time (IST) and a link to reschedule or cancel
Given an appointment whose reminder is due at 22:30 IST, When the booking is saved, Then the reminder is scheduled for 20:00 IST the same evening
Given an appointment whose reminder is due at 03:00 IST, When the booking is saved, Then the reminder is scheduled for 20:00 IST the evening before the due time

Given a reminder whose adjusted 20:00 time has already passed when the booking is made, When the booking is saved, Then the reminder goes at once if it is outside 21:00-08:00 IST, otherwise at 08:00 IST
Given an appointment booked less than 24 hours before it starts, When the booking is saved, Then no reminder is created and only the confirmation is sent
Given the reminder link, When the patient opens it, Then it opens that appointment where they can reschedule or cancel

estimate.rationale: 5 tasks (~18 h): a pure scheduling function with many boundary cases, a template, extension of on_booked and two test suites; logic-heavy but small surface.

open_questions: Q-009 is open: the quiet-hours rule (21:00-08:00, 20:00 evening, 08:00 fallback) is the default of SA-003/PD-004; plan_reminder takes all times from settings. If the client answers differently, only settings and the table-driven test cases change.
The reminder link opens the appointment page of feature 004 (reschedule or cancel); behaviour for a cancelled or past appointment is owned by E-004.

items.title: Reminders follow changes; change notices
items.description_md: When a patient cancels, no reminder is sent for that appointment and the patient gets a cancellation notice. When a patient reschedules, the old reminder is dropped, one reminder is set for the new time only, and the patient gets a change notice with the new details. These notices are the messages required by the cancel/reschedule flows. **Why this priority**: A reminder for a cancelled appointment is a hard failure of NFR-005 ("none sent for cancelled appointments") and would confuse patients; change notices complete the patient flow of feature 004. **Independent Test**: Book, then cancel before the reminder is due and verify no reminder is sent and a cancellation notice is; book, then reschedule and verify only one reminder exists, for the new time, and a change notice is sent. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a booked appointment with a pending reminder, **When** the patient or reception cancels it, **Then** the pending reminder is cancelled in the same change and never sent. 2. **Given** a reminder already claimed for sending, **When** the appointment is found cancelled at the last re-check, **Then** the reminder is not sent. 3. **Given** a booked appointment with a pending reminder, **When** it is rescheduled, **Then** the old reminder is cancelled and exactly one new reminder is scheduled for the new time (quiet-hours rule and less-than-24-hours rule apply). 4. **Given** a cancel or reschedule, **When** it is saved, **Then** the patient receives a notice in the chosen channel with the clinic, dentist, date and time (new date and time for a reschedule), even if reminders are switched off. 5. **Given** a reschedule to a time less than 24 hours ahead, **When** it is saved, **Then** no reminder is created and only the change notice is sent. ---

user_story.as_a: patient who cancels or reschedules an appointment
user_story.i_want: no reminder for a cancelled appointment, one reminder for the new time after a reschedule, and a notice telling me what changed
user_story.so_that: I am not confused by wrong reminders and know my change was saved

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a booked appointment with a pending reminder, When the patient or reception cancels it, Then the pending reminder is cancelled in the same change and never sent

Given a reschedule to a time less than 24 hours ahead, When it is saved, Then no reminder is created and only the change notice is sent

items.title: Stop reminders by replying STOP or through reception
items.description_md: A patient can stop reminders by replying STOP to a message, or by asking reception, who switch reminders off in the patient's record. From then on no reminders are sent, but confirmations of a booking or a change are still sent. Reception can switch reminders back on if the patient asks. **Why this priority**: Required by the messaging rules (NFR-011) and by the patient's rights; it must be live at go-live but depends on the sending path from stories 1-4. **Independent Test**: Post a signed STOP webhook for a test patient and check that their pending reminders are not sent and a following booking still gets a confirmation; switch the flag on from the reception record screen and check the same. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient with pending reminders, **When** the provider forwards their STOP reply, **Then** the patient's reminders are switched off at once and their pending reminders are cancelled (honoured well within 1 hour). 2. **Given** reminders switched off, **When** the patient books or changes an appointment, **Then** the confirmation or change notice is still sent and no reminder is created. 3. **Given** a receptionist on the patient's record screen, **When** they switch reminders off, **Then** the same effect applies as for STOP and the change is recorded with who did it and when. 4. **Given** a receptionist, **When** they switch reminders back on at the patient's request, **Then** future bookings get reminders again. 5. **Given** an incoming STOP webhook without a valid signature or from an unknown sender, **When** it is received, **Then** it is rejected and nothing changes. 6. **Given** the same STOP webhook delivered twice, **When** it is processed, **Then** the result is the same as once. ---

user_story.as_a: patient who does not want reminders
user_story.i_want: to stop them by replying STOP or by asking reception, while still getting confirmations and change notices
user_story.so_that: I stay in control of the messages I get
