items.title: Sign-in codes sent by SMS
items.description_md: When a patient asks for a sign-in code, the system sends it by SMS through the registered sender and template, as part of the request, and reports a clear error if it cannot be sent. This feature supplies only the sending; code rules (10 minutes, 5 tries, 15-minute wait) belong to the sign-in feature. **Why this priority**: Patients cannot sign in, and so cannot book, without it; it is a shared use of the same provider setup. **Independent Test**: Request a code for a test number against the sandbox SMS provider and check that exactly one SMS with the code is sent through the code template, and that a provider failure gives the patient a "try again" answer. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a valid phone number and sign-in allowed, **When** the patient asks for a code, **Then** one SMS with the code is sent through the registered code template before the request returns. 2. **Given** the provider is slow or failing, **When** the patient asks for a code, **Then** the request ends within the provider timeout with a clear "could not send, try again" answer and the failure is recorded without the code or the phone number in logs. 3. **Given** a sign-in code message, **When** it is stored, **Then** the code itself is not kept in readable form after sending. ---

user_story.i_want: to receive my sign-in code by SMS and get a clear answer if it cannot be sent
user_story.so_that: I can sign in and book

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a valid phone number and sign-in allowed, When the patient asks for a code, Then one SMS with the code is sent through the registered code template before the request returns

Given the provider is slow or failing, When the patient asks for a code, Then the request ends within the provider timeout with a clear "could not send, try again" answer and the failure is recorded without the code or the phone number in logs
Given a sign-in code message, When it is stored, Then the code itself is not kept in readable form after sending

estimate.rationale: 3 tasks (~12 h): one service method reusing the SMS adapter, a call site in the sign-in request, and tests; small but touches the auth flow of E-001.

open_questions: Sign-in codes need a DLT-registered code template (DEP-001): without approval real sign-in cannot go live on 2027-02-22 (RSK-001).
SMS provider not selected (ASM-009): the code is sent through the sandbox adapter until then.
Code rules (10 min, 5 tries, 15 min wait) are in E-001; this story only supplies sending and the error answer.

items.title: Reliable and compliant delivery operations
items.description_md: The operations team can trust that due messages go out on time and only through approved templates: delivery receipts update message status, a nightly check finds due messages that were never sent, an alert fires when reminders lag by 10 minutes, templates are chosen from configuration, and only the allowed fields reach the providers. The design leaves room for the Release 2 fallback and failed-reminder list. **Why this priority**: Needed to prove NFR-005 and NFR-011 in production, and to catch a stuck dispatcher before patients notice. **Independent Test**: Run the dispatcher with a failing provider and verify retries, circuit breaker and that the message stays queued; post receipts and check status; skip a due row and check the nightly check reports it; check the lag alert fires at 10 minutes. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** due messages, **When** the dispatcher runs every 30 seconds, **Then** each due message is claimed by exactly one worker, sent once, and marked sent with the provider message id. 2. **Given** a provider error, **When** a send fails, **Then** it is retried up to 3 attempts in all, with waits of 5 s and 30 s, and a provider call never lasts more than 5 s. 3. **Given** 5 provider failures within 1 minute, **When** the next message is due, **Then** sending to that provider pauses (message stays queued) and resumes after a probe succeeds. 4. **Given** a delivery receipt (SMS or WhatsApp) with a valid signature, **When** it arrives, **Then** the message status is updated; the same receipt twice, or one for an unknown message id, changes nothing. 5. **Given** a due message still unsent 10 minutes after its scheduled time, **When** the monitor runs, **Then** an alert is raised. 6. **Given** the nightly check, **When** it finds a due reminder without a message row, or a stuck row for a booked appointment, **Then** it creates or requeues it and logs the repair; it never sends for a cancelled appointment. 7. **Given** any outgoing message, **When** it is built, **Then** it uses the template id from configuration for that kind and channel and sends only clinic, dentist, date, time and link as template values. 8. **Given** message rows older than 90 days, **When** the retention job runs, **Then** they are deleted. ---

user_story.as_a: member of the operations team running the booking system
user_story.i_want: retries, a circuit breaker, delivery receipts, a lag alert, a nightly repair job and 90-day retention
user_story.so_that: due messages go out on time (99% within 15 minutes), only through approved templates, and stuck ones are found before patients notice

items.title: Add and manage family members
items.description_md: A signed-in patient opens "Family members" from their account and adds a person with a name and a birth year. They can see the list of people on the account (themselves first, then family members), correct a name or birth year, and remove a family member they no longer book for. An account holds at most 5 family members. **Why this priority**: Without family members on the account nothing else in this feature can be used. **Independent Test**: Sign in as a patient with no family members, add 5 people, try a sixth, edit one, remove one, and add a new one again. Delivers a working family list with no booking changes. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-in patient with fewer than 5 family members, **When** they add a family member with a valid name and a valid birth year, **Then** the person appears in the family list and can be chosen in later screens. 2. **Given** a patient who already has 5 family members, **When** they try to add another, **Then** the system refuses, explains that 5 is the limit, and the list is unchanged. 3. **Given** a patient adding a family member, **When** the name is empty, or the birth year is not a four-digit year, is in the future, or is more than 120 years ago, **Then** the system shows what is wrong next to the field and saves nothing. 4. **Given** a patient with a family member, **When** they correct the name or birth year, **Then** the change is saved and shown in the list and on that person's appointments. 5. **Given** a family member with no upcoming booked appointment, **When** the patient removes them, **Then** they leave the list, can no longer be chosen for new bookings, and the patient can add another family member in their place. 6. **Given** a family member with an upcoming booked appointment, **When** the patient tries to remove them, **Then** the system refuses and says to cancel those appointments first. (source: FR-006; Assumed, open question Q2) 7. **Given** the family feature is switched off, **When** any patient opens their account, **Then** no family screens or links are visible and the family operations are refused. ---

items.title: Choose who the visit is for when booking
items.description_md: In the booking flow, at the step "who and what", the patient chooses whether the visit is for themselves or for one of their family members, then continues with clinic and treatment as before. The booking records the person it is for. If the patient has no family members, the booking flow behaves as before (visit for themselves) without an extra choice. **Why this priority**: Booking for another person is the whole value of the feature for P-01. **Independent Test**: With one family member on the account, book a check-up choosing that family member; the booked screen and the saved appointment name that person. Book another choosing "myself". **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a signed-in patient with at least one family member, **When** they reach the "who and what" step, **Then** they see themselves and each family member as choices, with "myself" pre-selected. 2. **Given** a patient who chose a family member, **When** they confirm the booking, **Then** the appointment is saved for that person and the booked screen and the appointment page name that person. 3. **Given** a patient who has no family members, **When** they book, **Then** the visit is for themselves and no "who" choice is asked. 4. **Given** a request to book for a person who is not on the patient's own account (for example a changed id), **When** the booking is submitted, **Then** the system refuses it and no appointment is created. 5. **Given** a family member who was removed, **When** the patient books, **Then** that person is not offered and a booking for them is refused. 6. **Given** a family member who is blocked online after repeat no-shows, **When** the patient chooses them, **Then** the block message from the no-show rules applies to that person only, not to the account holder or other members. (source: FR-006; PD-007 handled by feature 006) ---

items.title: See family members' appointments, and only those
items.description_md: On "My appointments" the patient sees upcoming and past appointments for themselves and for every family member on the account, each showing the name of the person it is for. A patient never sees appointments of anyone who is not a person on their own account. **Why this priority**: Booking for family is hard to trust if the patient cannot see the result, and the privacy rule is mandatory; but the list can ship just after booking. **Independent Test**: Create appointments for the holder and two family members on one account and one appointment on another account. The first patient's list shows exactly three, with names; the second patient's list shows only theirs. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an account with appointments for the holder and for two family members, **When** the patient opens "My appointments", **Then** all of them are listed with status and the name of the person each is for. 2. **Given** two different accounts, **When** one patient opens an appointment of the other account, by list or by direct link, **Then** the system refuses and reveals nothing about it. 3. **Given** a family member who was removed but had past appointments, **When** the patient opens the list, **Then** the past appointments are still shown with that person's name. (source: FR-006; Assumed, open question Q2) 4. **Given** an account with family appointments, **When** the patient reschedules or cancels one of them within the usual 4-hour rule, **Then** it works exactly as for their own appointments. ---

items.title: Erase family member data and keep it out of logs
items.description_md: When a patient asks for their data to be deleted, the family members' names and birth years go with it. A deleted family member's appointments stay as anonymous rows so counts remain right. Names and birth years never appear in logs or error reports. **Why this priority**: Required by the privacy rule (NFR-007) but it builds on the existing erasure of the account and is used rarely. **Independent Test**: Erase an account with 3 family members; none of their names or birth years remain stored or findable, their appointments remain without personal link, and a search of the logs from the test run finds none of those values. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an account with family members, **When** the practice manager runs erasure for that account on request, **Then** every family member's name and birth year are removed or anonymised, and their appointments remain without a personal link. 2. **Given** a family member added, edited, removed or booked for, **When** the logs of that action are inspected, **Then** they contain ids and a correlation id but no name or birth year. 3. **Given** an account erased on request, **When** the patient signs in again with the same phone number, **Then** it is treated as a new account with no family members. ---

items.title: A repeat no-show patient cannot book or reschedule online
items.description_md: A patient (or a family member the patient books for) who has had 2 no-shows in the last 6 months is blocked from booking a new appointment online and from rescheduling an appointment online. Where they would book or change a time, the page tells them online booking is not available and shows the phone number of the clinic they were using. Appointments they already hold stay as they are. The count is kept per person: a family member's no-show counts against that family member, not against the account holder. Reception booking is never blocked. **Why this priority**: This is the point of the feature: repeat no-shows lose online booking so the chair is not left empty again and again. Without it nothing else in the feature has value. **Independent Test**: Mark two no-shows for one patient inside 6 months, then try to book and to reschedule online as that patient: both are refused with the clinic phone number; the patient's existing future appointment is unchanged; the same attempt for the account holder (who has no no-shows) succeeds; a receptionist can still book that patient. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient has 2 no-shows within the last 6 months, **When** they reach the slot-choosing step of online booking for a clinic, **Then** the page says online booking is not available and shows that clinic's phone number, and no slot can be confirmed. 2. **Given** a patient has 2 no-shows within the last 6 months and an upcoming appointment, **When** they try to reschedule it online, **Then** the change is refused, the page says to phone the clinic and shows the clinic's phone number, and the appointment keeps its original time and status. 3. **Given** a blocked patient has other upcoming appointments, **When** they open their appointment list, **Then** all those appointments are still listed as booked and can still be cancelled online within the normal cancel rule. 4. **Given** a family member has 2 no-shows and the account holder has none, **When** the account holder books for themselves, **Then** the booking succeeds; **and When** they book for the family member, **Then** it is refused with the phone-the-clinic message. 5. **Given** a patient has only 1 no-show in the last 6 months, or has 2 no-shows of which one is older than 6 months, **When** they book or reschedule online, **Then** it succeeds. 6. **Given** a patient is blocked, **When** a receptionist books or reschedules an appointment for them, **Then** it succeeds with no block check. 7. **Given** a patient whose 2 counted no-shows were the only reason for the block, **When** the older of the two passes 6 months of age, **Then** the next online booking attempt succeeds without any staff action. ---

user_story.i_want: to be told clearly when online booking or rescheduling is not available for me and to get the clinic's phone number
user_story.so_that: I know to phone the clinic, while my existing appointments stay as they are

items.title: Reception sees who is blocked
items.description_md: A receptionist sees at a glance that a patient is blocked from online booking: on the appointment in the day view and appointment panel, and in patient search results. The panel shows since when the patient is blocked and the dates of the no-shows that count. A patient who is not blocked shows nothing extra. **Why this priority**: Reception is the only place the block can be resolved; they must see it before they can decide to lift it. It depends on Story 1's block existing. **Independent Test**: Block a patient (two no-shows), open the day view, appointment panel and patient search as a receptionist: a "Blocked" marker and the block details show for that patient only, including a family member shown by their own name. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a blocked patient has an appointment in the clinic's day view, **When** the receptionist opens the day view, **Then** that appointment shows a "Blocked from online booking" marker. 2. **Given** a blocked patient, **When** the receptionist opens the appointment panel or finds the patient by phone number or name in patient search, **Then** the blocked state, the date the block started and the counted no-show dates are shown. 3. **Given** a patient that is not blocked, **When** the receptionist views the same screens, **Then** no blocked marker is shown. 4. **Given** a family member is blocked but the account holder is not, **When** the receptionist searches by the shared phone number, **Then** only the family member's entry shows the blocked marker. 5. **Given** the feature is switched off for the release, **When** a receptionist opens any screen, **Then** no blocked marker or lift control appears. ---

user_story.i_want: to see at a glance which patients are blocked from online booking, since when, and which no-shows count
user_story.so_that: I can decide whether to lift the block when the patient phones

items.title: Reception lifts a block and the count restarts
items.description_md: When a blocked patient phones and the clinic agrees, the receptionist lifts the block. The patient can book and reschedule online straight away. The count starts again from zero at the moment of the lift: only no-shows after that moment count towards a new block. The lift records who did it and when. **Why this priority**: Gives the clinic a fair way out of the block (Reception flow step 6). Needs Stories 1 and 2. **Independent Test**: Block a patient, lift the block as a receptionist, confirm the patient can book online at once, then mark one no-show (still not blocked) and a second (blocked again); the earlier two no-shows are never counted again. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a blocked patient, **When** the receptionist chooses "Lift block" and confirms, **Then** the blocked marker disappears and the lift is recorded with the receptionist's name and the time. 2. **Given** a block has just been lifted, **When** the patient books or reschedules online, **Then** it succeeds. 3. **Given** a block was lifted, **When** the patient then gets 1 new no-show, **Then** they are not blocked; **and When** they get a second new no-show, **Then** they are blocked again. 4. **Given** a patient is not blocked, **When** a receptionist looks at the patient, **Then** no lift control is offered, and a direct lift request is refused. 5. **Given** a user who is not a receptionist (a patient, a dentist), **When** they try to lift a block, **Then** it is refused. ---

user_story.i_want: to lift a patient's block when the patient phones and the clinic agrees, so the count starts again from zero
user_story.so_that: the patient can book and reschedule online straight away, and the lift is recorded with who and when

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a blocked patient, When the receptionist chooses "Lift block" and confirms, Then the blocked marker disappears and the lift is recorded with the receptionist's name and the time
Given a block has just been lifted, When the patient books or reschedules online, Then it succeeds

Given a patient is not blocked, When a receptionist looks at the patient, Then no lift control is offered, and a direct lift request is refused
Given a user who is not a receptionist (a patient, a dentist), When they try to lift a block, Then it is refused

items.title: The block follows no-show corrections
items.description_md: When a receptionist marks a no-show or undoes one (allowed the same day, PD-003), the patient's block state is recalculated at once. Marking the second no-show blocks the patient; undoing a no-show that caused a block removes the block. **Why this priority**: Without it, a mistaken no-show (undone the same day) would leave a patient wrongly blocked, which would harm patients and trust. It builds on Story 1. **Independent Test**: Mark a second no-show for a patient with one earlier no-show: the patient becomes blocked immediately. Undo that no-show the same day: the patient is unblocked and can book online. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a patient has 1 no-show in the last 6 months, **When** a receptionist marks a second no-show for them, **Then** the patient is blocked from online booking immediately. 2. **Given** a patient was blocked by their second no-show, **When** the receptionist undoes that no-show the same day, **Then** the patient is no longer blocked. 3. **Given** a patient was blocked, lifted, and then had one new no-show, **When** that no-show is undone, **Then** the count is zero and nothing else changes. 4. **Given** a patient has no-shows for appointments of different family members, **When** a no-show is marked or undone, **Then** only the person the appointment was for is recounted. ---

user_story.i_want: the patient's block to be recalculated the moment I mark or undo a no-show
user_story.so_that: a second no-show blocks at once and a mistaken no-show undone the same day does not leave the patient wrongly blocked

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a patient has 1 no-show in the last 6 months, When a receptionist marks a second no-show for them, Then the patient is blocked from online booking immediately
Given a patient was blocked by their second no-show, When the receptionist undoes that no-show the same day, Then the patient is no longer blocked
Given a patient was blocked, lifted, and then had one new no-show, When that no-show is undone, Then the count is zero and nothing else changes
Given a patient has no-shows for appointments of different family members, When a no-show is marked or undone, Then only the person the appointment was for is recounted

ESTIMATE CHECK (scope/estimate.md): estimate.md has no separate line for the fallback and failed list; they are part of MOD-07 'Reminders and messages', 15-24 person-days (L, medium confidence; drivers include 'fallback to SMS' and 'delivery failures'). Backlog: E-009 = 23 SP = 138 h = 17.25 pd (8 h/day); E-006 + E-009 together = 65 SP = 48.75 pd against MOD-07 15-24 pd, i.e. 2.0-3.25x. LARGE GAP: re-baseline or cut scope. items.title: A failed WhatsApp reminder is sent once by SMS
items.description_md: A patient chose WhatsApp for messages. Their reminder cannot be delivered on WhatsApp (the provider reports an error after all attempts, or reports a failed delivery receipt). The system then sends the same reminder once by SMS so the patient is still reminded. **Why this priority**: A reminder that never arrives defeats the goal of fewer no-shows; this is the core of the feature. **Independent Test**: Make a WhatsApp reminder fail (provider error after 3 attempts, or a failed receipt) and check that exactly one SMS reminder is created and sent for it, even when the failed receipt is delivered several times. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a due WhatsApp reminder for a booked appointment and the fallback switch on, **When** the WhatsApp provider returns an error on all 3 attempts, **Then** one SMS reminder with the same content is created and sent to the patient's phone number. 2. **Given** a WhatsApp reminder that was accepted by the provider, **When** a failed delivery receipt arrives later, **Then** one SMS reminder is created and sent. 3. **Given** a WhatsApp reminder that already has its SMS fallback, **When** the same failed receipt is received again (replayed), **Then** no second SMS is created or sent. 4. **Given** a WhatsApp reminder that was delivered, **When** a delivery receipt arrives, **Then** no SMS is sent. 5. **Given** an SMS fallback has been sent, **When** it is delivered, **Then** the appointment is not marked "reminder failed". ---

user_story.as_a: patient who chose WhatsApp for messages
user_story.i_want: my appointment reminder to be sent once by SMS when WhatsApp cannot deliver it
user_story.so_that: I am still reminded and do not miss my appointment

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a due WhatsApp reminder for a booked appointment and the fallback switch on, When the WhatsApp provider returns an error on all 3 attempts, Then one SMS reminder with the same content is created and sent to the patient's phone number
Given a WhatsApp reminder that was accepted by the provider, When a failed delivery receipt arrives later, Then one SMS reminder is created and sent
Given a WhatsApp reminder that already has its SMS fallback, When the same failed receipt is received again (replayed), Then no second SMS is created or sent
Given a WhatsApp reminder that was delivered, When a delivery receipt arrives, Then no SMS is sent
Given an SMS fallback has been sent, When it is delivered, Then the appointment is not marked "reminder failed"

items.title: The fallback respects STOP, cancellations and the switch
items.description_md: The fallback never sends an SMS the patient has asked not to receive, never for an appointment that has since been cancelled, and can be switched off without a new release because the client has not agreed to it. **Why this priority**: These are compliance, cost and trust guards around Story 1; a fallback SMS to an opted-out patient breaks the STOP promise. **Independent Test**: Fail a WhatsApp reminder in each situation (patient opted out, appointment cancelled, switch off) and check that no SMS is created and nothing wrong is shown to reception. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a failed WhatsApp reminder for a patient who has switched reminders off (STOP or by reception), **When** the fallback would run, **Then** no SMS is created. 2. **Given** a failed WhatsApp reminder whose appointment has been cancelled, **When** the fallback would run, **Then** no SMS is created. 3. **Given** the fallback switch is off, **When** a WhatsApp reminder finally fails, **Then** no SMS is created and the appointment is marked "reminder failed" so reception can phone the patient. 4. **Given** the system is installed without any setting for the switch, **When** a WhatsApp reminder finally fails, **Then** the fallback behaves as on. 5. **Given** the switch was turned off while an SMS fallback was waiting to be sent, **When** the sending is due, **Then** the SMS is not sent and the appointment is marked "reminder failed". ---

user_story.as_a: patient who has switched reminders off (and as the clinic paying for messages)
user_story.i_want: the fallback never to send an SMS after STOP, for a cancelled appointment, or when the fallback is switched off
user_story.so_that: my opt-out is respected and the clinic can disable the extra-cost fallback without a new release

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a failed WhatsApp reminder for a patient who has switched reminders off (STOP or by reception), When the fallback would run, Then no SMS is created
Given a failed WhatsApp reminder whose appointment has been cancelled, When the fallback would run, Then no SMS is created
Given the fallback switch is off, When a WhatsApp reminder finally fails, Then no SMS is created and the appointment is marked "reminder failed" so reception can phone the patient
Given the system is installed without any setting for the switch, When a WhatsApp reminder finally fails, Then the fallback behaves as on
Given the switch was turned off while an SMS fallback was waiting to be sent, When the sending is due, Then the SMS is not sent and the appointment is marked "reminder failed"

items.title: An appointment is marked "reminder failed" when the SMS also fails
items.description_md: When the SMS fallback also cannot be delivered, the appointment is marked "reminder failed", so that nobody assumes the patient was reminded. **Why this priority**: Without this mark, reception cannot know whom to phone (Story 4 depends on it). **Independent Test**: Fail a WhatsApp reminder and then its SMS fallback (provider error or failed receipt) and check that the appointment shows "reminder failed" once, and that replayed receipts change nothing. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** an SMS fallback for a failed WhatsApp reminder, **When** the SMS provider returns an error on all attempts, **Then** the appointment is marked "reminder failed". 2. **Given** an SMS fallback accepted by the provider, **When** a failed delivery receipt arrives, **Then** the appointment is marked "reminder failed". 3. **Given** an appointment already marked "reminder failed", **When** the same failed receipt is received again, **Then** the mark is unchanged and no further message is sent. 4. **Given** the appointment was cancelled before the SMS failed, **When** the SMS failure is recorded, **Then** the appointment is not shown as "reminder failed" to reception. 5. **Given** a "reminder failed" mark, **When** a later delivery receipt says the earlier message was in fact delivered, **Then** the mark is removed. ---

user_story.i_want: an appointment to be marked reminder failed when neither WhatsApp nor the SMS fallback could be delivered
user_story.so_that: nobody assumes the patient was reminded and I know whom to phone

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an SMS fallback for a failed WhatsApp reminder, When the SMS provider returns an error on all attempts, Then the appointment is marked "reminder failed"
Given an SMS fallback accepted by the provider, When a failed delivery receipt arrives, Then the appointment is marked "reminder failed"
Given an appointment already marked "reminder failed", When the same failed receipt is received again, Then the mark is unchanged and no further message is sent
Given the appointment was cancelled before the SMS failed, When the SMS failure is recorded, Then the appointment is not shown as "reminder failed" to reception
Given a "reminder failed" mark, When a later delivery receipt says the earlier message was in fact delivered, Then the mark is removed

items.title: Reception gets tomorrow's reminders-failed list
items.description_md: A receptionist asks for the list of tomorrow's appointments, at their own clinic, whose reminder failed, with what is needed to phone the patient (patient name, phone number, time, dentist, treatment). **Why this priority**: This is the human fallback that makes the failure visible and actionable; it relies on Story 3. **Independent Test**: Create appointments for tomorrow and the day after at two clinics, some marked "reminder failed", and check that a receptionist of clinic A sees only clinic A's tomorrow appointments that are marked, ordered by time. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** tomorrow has 3 booked appointments at the receptionist's clinic marked "reminder failed", **When** the receptionist requests the list, **Then** all 3 are listed in time order with patient name, phone number, time, dentist and treatment. 2. **Given** an appointment marked "reminder failed" at another clinic, **When** a receptionist of this clinic requests the list, **Then** it is not shown. 3. **Given** an appointment marked "reminder failed" for a day other than tomorrow, **When** the list is requested, **Then** it is not shown. 4. **Given** a "reminder failed" appointment that has since been cancelled, **When** the list is requested, **Then** it is not shown. 5. **Given** no reminders failed, **When** the list is requested, **Then** an empty list is returned, not an error. 6. **Given** a patient, dentist or practice manager signs in, **When** they request the list, **Then** the request is refused. ---

items.title: "Reminders failed" screen for reception
items.description_md: In the afternoon the receptionist opens the "Reminders failed" screen for tomorrow, sees the patients to phone, and works down the list. The screen is hidden until Release 2 is switched on. **Why this priority**: Presents Story 4; the list is useful as soon as the screen exists, but the screen can follow the data. **Independent Test**: Sign in as a receptionist with the Release 2 flag on and off; check that the entry and the screen appear only when on, and that the list matches the data. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the Release 2 flag is on and a receptionist is signed in, **When** they open "Reminders failed", **Then** tomorrow's failed reminders of their clinic are shown with a phone number per patient. 2. **Given** the Release 2 flag is off, **When** a receptionist uses the application, **Then** no "Reminders failed" entry is shown and its address shows the standard not-found page. 3. **Given** there are none, **When** the screen opens, **Then** a plain message says no reminders failed for tomorrow. 4. **Given** the list cannot be loaded, **When** the screen opens, **Then** an error message with a retry action is shown. 5. **Given** a dentist, patient or practice manager is signed in, **When** they browse the application, **Then** they see no "Reminders failed" entry. ---

items.title: No-show report per clinic and month
items.description_md: Manager sees no-shows and rate per clinic for the last 12 months, on screen. RELEASE 2 (DL-2, due 2027-03-19, not hard). PRD ids: FR-032.
open_questions: ESTIMATE CHECK (scope/estimate.md, 1 SP = 6 h, 8 h per person-day): E-010 = 10 SP = 60 h = 7.5 pd against MOD-08 3-5 pd (1.5-2.5x the range; above the high end). Flag: re-baseline or cut scope (decision for the Delivery Manager).

items.title: Monthly no-show figures per clinic
items.description_md: The practice manager asks the system for the no-show figures of every clinic for each of the last 12 months. For each clinic and month the system returns the number of no-shows, the number of appointments that were not cancelled, and the no-show rate (no-shows ÷ appointments that were not cancelled). Walk-ins count like any other appointment. Appointments cancelled by the patient and appointments cancelled by the clinic are both left out of the denominator. Months follow India time (IST). Appointments whose personal details were anonymised after 24 months still count. **Why this priority**: This is the whole business value of the feature: the practice manager can see where no-shows happen and whether they fall. Without the figures there is nothing to show. **Independent Test**: Load appointments in different statuses for two clinics across several months, ask for the report, and compare each number and rate with a hand count. Can be tested without any screen. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a clinic had 40 appointments in a month, of which 4 were no-shows, 6 were cancelled by the patient and 2 were cancelled by the clinic, **When** the practice manager requests the report, **Then** that clinic and month show 4 no-shows and a rate of 4 ÷ 32 = 12.5%. 2. **Given** a walk-in that was booked at reception and marked arrived, and another walk-in marked as a no-show, **When** the report is requested, **Then** both are counted in the denominator and the no-show is counted as a no-show. 3. **Given** two clinics, **When** the report is requested, **Then** each clinic has its own row of 12 months and the figures of one clinic never include appointments of the other. 4. **Given** an appointment starting at 23:30 IST on the last day of a month (which is already the next day in UTC), **When** the report is requested, **Then** it is counted in the IST month it started in. 5. **Given** an appointment in the 12-month window whose patient details have been anonymised (after 24 months, or after a deletion request), **When** the report is requested, **Then** it still counts in its month and status. 6. **Given** a clinic with no appointments, or only cancelled appointments, in a month, **When** the report is requested, **Then** that month shows 0 no-shows and no rate (not a division error). ---

user_story.i_want: the number of no-shows and the no-show rate for each clinic and each of the last 12 months
user_story.so_that: I can see where no-shows happen and whether they fall, and a baseline is available to set a target

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a clinic had 40 appointments in a month, of which 4 were no-shows, 6 were cancelled by the patient and 2 were cancelled by the clinic, When the practice manager requests the report, Then that clinic and month show 4 no-shows and a rate of 4 ÷ 32 = 12.5%. (source: FR-032)

Given a walk-in that was booked at reception and marked arrived, and another walk-in marked as a no-show, When the report is requested, Then both are counted in the denominator and the no-show is counted as a no-show. (source: FR-032)
Given two clinics, When the report is requested, Then each clinic has its own row of 12 months and the figures of one clinic never include appointments of the other. (source: FR-032)

Given an appointment starting at 23:30 IST on the last day of a month (which is already the next day in UTC), When the report is requested, Then it is counted in the IST month it started in. (source: FR-032)

Given an appointment in the 12-month window whose patient details have been anonymised (after 24 months, or after a deletion request), When the report is requested, Then it still counts in its month and status. (source: FR-032)
Given a clinic with no appointments, or only cancelled appointments, in a month, When the report is requested, Then that month shows 0 no-shows and no rate (not a division error). (source: FR-032)

items.title: No-show report screen for the practice manager
items.description_md: The practice manager opens the "no-show report" screen from the staff menu and sees a table per clinic: one row per month for the last 12 months, newest first, with the number of no-shows, the number of appointments that were not cancelled, and the rate as a percentage. The screen is read only and has no export. While the feature is not switched on, the screen is not offered at all. **Why this priority**: The figures are of no use to the manager until they can read them on screen; this is the only way the report is delivered (export is a non-goal). **Independent Test**: Sign in as the practice manager with the feature switched on, open the report screen and check that each clinic shows 12 monthly rows that match the report figures; switch the feature off and check that the screen is not offered. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** the practice manager is signed in and the report is switched on, **When** they open the no-show report from the menu, **Then** they see every clinic with 12 monthly rows showing no-shows, non-cancelled appointments and rate. 2. **Given** a month with no rate (no non-cancelled appointments), **When** the table is shown, **Then** the rate cell shows a dash and not 0% or an error. 3. **Given** a third clinic has been added as data, **When** the screen is opened, **Then** the third clinic appears without any change to the screen. 4. **Given** the report is switched off, **When** the practice manager looks at the menu or opens the screen address directly, **Then** the screen is not offered and the address shows "not found". 5. **Given** the figures cannot be loaded, **When** the screen is opened, **Then** the manager sees a plain error message with a retry button, and no partial figures. 6. **Given** the report screen, **When** the manager looks for a download or print-to-file option, **Then** there is none: the report is on screen only. ---

user_story.i_want: to open a read-only no-show report screen from the staff menu showing a 12-month table per clinic
user_story.so_that: I can read each clinic's no-shows and rate at a glance without exporting anything

acceptance_criteria.text: Given the practice manager is signed in and the report is switched on, When they open the no-show report from the menu, Then they see every clinic with 12 monthly rows showing no-shows, non-cancelled appointments and rate. (source: FR-032)

Given a third clinic has been added as data, When the screen is opened, Then the third clinic appears without any change to the screen. (source: FR-032)
Given the report is switched off, When the practice manager looks at the menu or opens the screen address directly, Then the screen is not offered and the address shows "not found". (source: FR-032)
Given the figures cannot be loaded, When the screen is opened, Then the manager sees a plain error message with a retry button, and no partial figures. (source: FR-032)
Given the report screen, When the manager looks for a download or print-to-file option, Then there is none: the report is on screen only. (source: FR-032)

items.title: Only the practice manager can read the report
items.description_md: Receptionists, dentists and patients cannot see the report or its figures, neither through the screen nor by asking the system directly. Only the practice manager sees all clinics. **Why this priority**: The report is management information, and the roles rule (FR-004) is a security baseline. It is P2 because the figures are only harmful if the role check is missing, and the check is cheap to build together with story 1. **Independent Test**: Request the report as each of the four roles, and without signing in; only the practice manager gets figures. **Acceptance Scenarios**: 1. **Given** a receptionist is signed in, **When** they request the report directly, **Then** the request is refused and no figures are returned. 2. **Given** a dentist or a patient is signed in, **When** they request the report directly, **Then** the request is refused. 3. **Given** nobody is signed in, **When** the report is requested, **Then** the request is refused as not signed in. 4. **Given** a receptionist or a dentist is signed in, **When** they look at the menu, **Then** there is no no-show report entry. ---

user_story.i_want: the no-show report to be visible and readable only by me, not by receptionists, dentists, patients or unsigned callers
user_story.so_that: management figures stay confidential and the roles rule (FR-004) is kept

Given a receptionist or a dentist is signed in, When they look at the menu, Then there is no no-show report entry. (source: FR-032)
